market_context.summary: Stagflation with a tightening central bank, and the book was built for the opposite. The Fed HIKED 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (first hike since 2023, 12-0) with a dot-plot median carrying one more in 2026; the 10-year touched 5.342% this week, its highest since early 2002 and above the 2007 peak, closing the week at 5.24% against a 3.88% effective funds rate — a 136bp term premium. Core PCE has run above 3% every month of 2026 and CPIAUCSL rose 0.40% m/m, while the labour market loosened: September payrolls +29,000 and unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%. Equities rallied on that weakness (S&P 500 +0.2% to 7,666.45) because weak labour cools hike bets; October is priced ~84% hold, with December the market's preferred hike date at ~65%. The cleanest read on the regime is that gold and oil, both 'inflation hedges', went opposite ways: gold fell 8.5% in September on the real-yield repricing while Brent rose 54% y/y on a pure supply shock — a third US carrier group heading to the Middle East, three tankers attacked transiting Hormuz, and Ukrainian strikes removing at least 30% of Russian refining capacity. The market is trading the discount rate, not the inflation print. The squeeze is specifically in middle distillates: the diesel crack hit an all-time $102/bbl against a ~$20 norm, with US distillate inventories 14% below the five-year seasonal average, the lowest seasonal level on record. Crypto de-risked broadly overnight (BTC -2.1%, high-beta alts -3 to -5%).

recommendations.thesis: The record refined-product squeeze is being traded entirely from the refiner side, and the consumer side is where the mispricing sits. The diesel crack hit an all-time $102/bbl, roughly five times normal, because Ukrainian strikes removed at least 30% of Russian refining capacity and the facilities knocked offline skew toward diesel and jet rather than gasoline; US distillate inventories are 14% below the five-year seasonal average, the lowest seasonal level on record. Jet fuel is the same middle distillate: $181.46/bbl on 2026-09-17, +84% y/y and 19% above IATA's $152 forecast. American is the carrier least able to absorb it — it guides FY2026 to an adjusted loss of $0.65 to a profit of $0.65 while Delta, which owns the Trainer refinery and is structurally long this crack, affirmed $6.50-7.50. A second and independent driver compounds it: the 10-year touched 5.342% this week, its highest since early 2002, and AAL carried $25,164 million of debt and finance leases at 2026-06-30, refinancing aircraft in July at a 6.30% coupon. Fuel and refinancing hit the same P&L.
recommendations.key_risk: DELTA REPORTS 2026-10-09, FOUR SESSIONS BEFORE AAL AND INSIDE THIS HOLDING PERIOD (fetched finnhub calendar, bmo). This is the risk the idea was missing. The thesis' central evidence is the guidance gap — DAL affirmed $6.50-7.50 while AAL guides -$0.65 to +$0.65 — but both figures are July prints, and Delta resets its half of the comparison on 10/09. A Delta beat with confident fare-pass-through commentary lifts the whole group and can take out the 14.40 stop before the AAL catalyst the trade is built on ever arrives; the single piece of evidence carrying the idea has a known expiry date ahead of its own resolution. Short interest is UNKNOWN — market_data.py short failed on four attempts with a nasdaq read timeout and the tool has no fallback — so I cannot rule out that this is a crowded short, and a crowded short in a $13 airline is squeeze fuel into a print. The single most likely way this loses is a Middle East de-escalation headline: the crack spread is a war premium, and the same carrier-strike-group news that created it unwinds it fast. Airlines have also repeatedly passed fuel through via fares and cut capacity faster than bears expect, and AAL is already 31% off its high, so a great deal of bad news is priced. The debt leg of the thesis ($25.2bn of debt and finance leases, aircraft refinanced in July at 6.30%) is a multi-year drag, not a 15-session driver, and should not be read as a second reason to be short over this horizon.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that fares and capacity cuts have absorbed every fuel spike this cycle and AAL at -31% off its high is the sector's obvious short, which usually means it is the crowded one. The answer is the guidance gap rather than an assertion: on the same fuel curve Delta affirmed $6.50-7.50 and American guides to a range straddling zero, and the street has moved with it — AAL analyst bullish share is 50.0% and falling 6.7 points while DAL sits at 90.6% and unchanged. Pass-through is working for the carrier with a refinery and premium mix; it is not working here.

READ THIS BEFORE READING THE RANKINGS: ONLY ONE OF THESE 15 ROWS IS NEW RISK. AAL (rank 1) is the single new idea. The other 14 are position management against a book of 16 open positions — 6 holds with levels unchanged (DINO, PFE, EEM, XLE, SNX, XLU), 7 CLOSES (GDX, LULU, NKE, LCII, KHC, BCC, CCJ), and 1 stop amendment (SVRA, widened 4.60 -> 4.30). Do not read 15 rows as 15 opportunities; the day in one line is close the falling-rate book, keep energy and defensives, add one short. The exits are a deliberate regime response, not a reaction to drawdown: the book was long gold, long building products, long de-rated discretionary and long packaged food — a falling-rate book held into a Fed that hiked on 2026-09-16.

WHY ONLY ONE NEW IDEA. Five orthogonal lanes were researched and all five were dropped, each with its evidence logged: crypto (readings genuinely balanced and the sources conflict on the one number that matters — October hike odds quoted at 64%, below 50%, and 84% hold by three different sources); brokers/custodians (blocked by the correlation cap, not by merit); staffing shorts MAN/RHI/KFY (falsified by company data — RHI's revenue decline is NARROWING, -5.6% to -2.8% y/y, with perm placement +6.3%); aluminium (the hypothesis was backwards, supply is restarting, and the short it implied was already priced into a -50% stock on its low); managed care (the bear case is in the company's own guidance, therefore priced). Refiners VLO/MPC/PSX were rejected on price despite the thesis being right. Nothing was padded to raise the count.

WHAT SYNTHESIS RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. All 15 prices were re-quoted and all 8 ATR14 values re-fetched: every one matched the research notes exactly. All 8 reward-to-risk ratios were recomputed from entry, target and stop and all 8 matched the claimed figure to within 0.01. All 8 expectancies are positive and every win_probability beats its 1/(1+R:R) baseline with the claimed edge inside the 20-point limit (AAL +14.4pt, DINO +19.8pt, SVRA +4.6pt, PFE +5.5pt, XLE +13.0pt, XLU +12.5pt, SNX +17.6pt, EEM +17.4pt). Every idea's conviction score equals its count of distinct evidence kinds; none needed lowering.

RATIOS CLUSTERED AT THE FLOOR — AND WHY IT IS NOT THE USUAL PROBLEM. Four ratios sit just above the 2.0 swing floor: DINO 2.10, XLU 2.07, SNX 2.08, XLE 2.13. That is normally the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Here these are INHERITED levels on positions opened between 2026-08-15 and 2026-09-24 and held UNCHANGED today; no target or stop was moved to make any of them pass, and research explicitly refused to raise DINO's target into a record print. Judge the clustering as a property of how the book was opened, not of today's work.

TWO STOPS FAIL THE ATR FLOOR ON AN ENTRY-BASED MEASURE, AND WERE DELIBERATELY NOT MASSAGED. DINO's 97.75 stop is 1.85 ATR below its 107.50 entry and SNX's 242.50 is 1.33 ATR below its 260.00 entry, both inside the 2.0 swing floor (independently recomputed here). Both are filled, profitable positions whose stops are comfortably clear of the floor measured from current price (2.97 and 2.72 ATR). DINO is the instructive case: the two floors are in direct conflict and there is no honest way to satisfy both — widening the stop to 96.98 clears the ATR floor but drops reward-to-risk to 1.93, under the 2.0 floor, and the only arithmetic passing both is a higher target, which is precisely the 'targets nudged until they passed' failure this repo has already shipped once. So both levels were left alone and the conflict is disclosed inside each idea. If 2b/2d demote DINO or SNX for stop distance, that is the validator working correctly on a defect in how the position was opened; it should not be fixed by moving a number.

PFE's 14.4:1 RATIO IS AN ARTIFACT AND ITS RANK IS INFLATED BY IT. The 42.00 target is a legacy valuation number 51% above spot, paired with a stop only 4.3% away on the lowest ATR in the book (1.69%); that combination manufactures a flattering ratio rather than an edge. Research's own self-audit caught the consequence: win_probability had been claimed at 0.40 against a 6.5% baseline, a 33.5-point asserted edge, and was corrected to 0.12. Because ranking is conviction-then-ratio, that artifact ratio places PFE at rank 4 — that is the rule applied mechanically and should NOT be read as the fourth most attractive idea on the page. It costs nothing in practice: every conviction-3 row here is a hold or a close carrying 'do not add', so rank order directs no new capital. Only AAL does.

THE SEVEN EXITS ARE ENDORSED IN FULL AND HAVE BEEN MOVED TO THE WATCHLIST TO STOP THE TRACKER MIS-RECORDING THEM. GDX, LULU, NKE, LCII, KHC, BCC and CCJ now sit at the top of the watchlist, each note beginning CLOSE IN FULL with its price, basis and reason. This is not a rejection and the notes say so. The schema has no exit action, so a close was encoded as direction=sell with target and stop null, and that has two consequences neither of which is the exit being questioned. (1) All seven FAIL mechanical validation on 'entry or target is missing', so phase 2d --enforce would have demoted them anyway, under the auto-generated note 'Demoted by validation... Republish only once the numbers check out' — the morning's single most important instruction, published as though it had been turned down. (2) Worse, if they are merged they do not close anything: merge_report keys on (symbol, direction), so ('GDX','sell') does not match the open ('GDX','buy'), and a close instruction opens a brand-new PENDING position instead. THIS HAS ALREADY HAPPENED AND IS IN THE RECORD. state/open_positions.json carries ('LULU','sell','open'), ('NKE','sell','open') and ('GLD','sell','pending') from the 2026-09-08 run — three close instructions now held as positions, two of them crediting the book +4.72% and +8.46% for exits, alongside the longs they were meant to close, and one exit filed as 'never filled'. Today's report would have added five more and amended the LULU and NKE phantoms. Two fixes are needed and neither belongs to the red team: an exit action in the schema that validate_report and positions_from_report both understand, and a one-off pass over the stored history for the three existing phantom sell rows, in the manner of scripts/dedupe_positions.py. Until then an exit must not be published as a recommendation.

DOWNGRADED, six. Both 5s come down to 4 and four 3s come down to 2. Every one of these clears the project's conviction floor at its new score, so nothing was cut for the count; what follows is why the old score was not paid for. AAL 5->4: the report's own key_risk names crowding as the most likely way it loses and short interest could not be fetched at all, so the first-order input to a $13 airline short into a print is simply unknown — and see the Delta point below. DINO 5->4: two of its four confirmations are weaker than their labels. The primary_document entry cites a Yahoo Finance article rather than a filing, and the valuation_anchor cites a 2026-07-23 Forbes piece to anchor an October crack level while arguing in a circle — the record crack is used to justify both the thesis and the target. PFE 3->2 and SNX 3->2: in each case BOTH evidence entries cite the same single fetch — nasdaq.com/.../pfe/historical twice, nasdaq.com/.../snx/historical twice — relabelled technical_level and positioning. That is one confirmation wearing two kinds, which is the exact inflation the distinct-kinds rule exists to stop, and synthesis's claim that 'every idea's conviction score equals its count of distinct evidence kinds' is not true of either (nor of DINO at 5-on-4 or SVRA at 2-on-1; the real rule, N-1 kinds, is met throughout). EEM 3->2: its counter_argument_answered entry does not answer the counter-argument, it concedes it — 'the objection is not dismissed, it is accepted' — so the idea rests on one confirmation, a technical reading, and its own key_risk calls the thesis 'price is going up'. XLE 3->2: of two confirmations one is about Brent rather than about XLE, and the only XLE-specific evidence reads against the direction (below SMA20, 5.06% off its high while refiners ran 70-110% off their lows). Holding an instrument that is not responding to a driver up 54% y/y is the weakest leg of the refined-product cluster, which is why it is the one marked down.
